title: 生查子·关山魂梦长
title_en: Sheng Zha Zi: Long Are the Dreams Across Mountain Passes
author: 王观

form.en: ci to the tune Sheng Zha Zi

glosses.zh: 关山：关口和山岭，指路途遥远、隔着重重山关。
glosses.en: guān shān: mountain passes and ranges; a long road with many mountains in between.

glosses.zh: 魂梦长：在梦里走了很远很远的路去找对方。
glosses.en: hún mèng cháng: in dreams the soul travels a long, long way to find the loved one.

glosses.zh: 塞（sài）雁：从北方边塞飞来的大雁。古人传说大雁能帮人带信。
glosses.en: sài yàn: wild geese from the northern frontier. People said geese could carry letters.

glosses.zh: 两鬓（bìn）：脸两旁靠近耳朵的头发。
glosses.en: liǎng bìn: the hair on both sides of the face, near the ears.

glosses.zh: 可怜：可爱，让人疼惜。青：黑色。可怜青：两鬓还是乌黑的，人还年轻。
glosses.en: kě lián qīng: kě lián here means lovely, dear; qīng means black. The hair is still black; the person is still young.
xiāng sī: missing someone far away.
guī bàng: to come back and stand close to. Bàng means near, beside.

glosses.zh: 碧纱窗：糊着绿纱的窗子，这里指心上人住的房间。
glosses.en: bì shā chuāng: a window covered with green gauze; here, the room of the loved one.

glosses.zh: 人人：宋代口语里对亲爱的人的称呼，就像“亲爱的”。
glosses.en: rén rén: in Song-dynasty speech, a loving name for a dear one, like "my dear".

translation.zh: 隔着重重关山，我在梦里走了很远的路。
translation.en: Across many mountain passes, my dreams travel a long way.

translation.zh: 北边飞来的大雁，却很少带来你的信。
translation.en: The geese from the frontier bring few letters from you.

translation.zh: 我两鬓的头发本来还那么黑，
translation.en: The hair at my temples was still so black,

translation.zh: 只想你一夜，就好像老了许多。
translation.en: yet one night of missing you seems to make me old.

translation.zh: 等我回去，靠在那绿纱窗旁，
translation.en: When I come home and stand by your green-gauze window,

translation.zh: 我要把心里话说给亲爱的你听：
translation.en: I will tell you, my dear, what is in my heart:

translation.zh: 怎么也比不上相聚的好。
translation.en: nothing is as good as being together.

background.zh: 这首词写一个在远方的人思念家中的爱人。几乎一样的一首词也收在晏几道的词集里，只有几个字不同：“塞雁音书”作“鱼雁音尘”，“一夜”作“只为”，“归傍”作“归梦”。到底是谁写的，历来说法不一，很多选本把它算作晏几道的作品。写作时间不详。词牌“生查子”的“查”读 zhā。
background.en: This ci is about someone far from home who misses the one he loves. An almost identical ci appears in the collected works of Yan Jidao, with only a few words changed. Scholars have long disagreed about who wrote it, and many anthologies give it to Yan Jidao. When it was written is not known. In the tune name Sheng Zha Zi, the middle word is read zhā.

author_note.zh: 王观，字通叟，北宋词人，做过官，后来被罢免，自号“逐客”。他的词语言活泼，常用口语，构思新巧，最有名的是《卜算子·送鲍浩然之浙东》里的“水是眼波横，山是眉峰聚”。这首词也很口语化，“人人”“真个”都是当时人说话用的词。
author_note.en: Wang Guan, also called Tongsou, was a Northern Song ci poet. He served as an official, was later dismissed, and called himself "the Banished Guest". His ci use lively, everyday speech and clever ideas. His most famous lines say "the water is the glance of her eyes, the hills are her gathered brows". This ci is also close to speech: rén rén and zhēn gè were words people used in daily talk.

appreciation.zh: 上片写远方的思念：路远，只能在梦里去找；信少，连大雁都不帮忙。“两鬓可怜青，一夜相思老”是全词最动人的地方，头发明明还黑，人却好像一夜之间老了，这是夸张，却把想念的苦说得很真切。下片换成想象：等我回去，站在你窗前，要对你说什么呢？说的话非常简单，就是“分开真难受，还是在一起好”。没有华丽的词，像普通人说的大白话，反而让人觉得真诚可信。
appreciation.en: The first half is about missing someone far away. The road is long, so he can only look for her in dreams. Letters are few; even the geese do not help. The most moving lines are about his hair: it is still black, yet one night of longing seems to make him old. It is an exaggeration, but it makes the pain of missing someone feel real. The second half imagines going home. Standing by her window, what will he say? Something very simple: being apart is hard, being together is better. There are no fancy words. It sounds like ordinary talk, and that is why it feels honest.

uncertain.zh: 这首词的作者有争议：一说是王观，一说是晏几道，很多选本归于晏几道，而且字句和晏几道集中的那首几乎相同。
uncertain.en: The authorship is disputed. Some sources give it to Wang Guan, others to Yan Jidao, and many anthologies follow Yan Jidao, whose version is almost identical.
